narrative: After hours on ENG-WS-22, the engineer d.coleman logged in interactively (security.evtx.jsonl:1) and, using valid credentials, robocopied the entire \\ENG-FS-01\IP_Designs share to a local staging folder (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:2, security.evtx.jsonl:5, netflow.csv:2). The collected data was packed into a password-protected 7-Zip archive designs.zip (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:3, filemod.csv:1). A SanDisk USB mass-storage drive was connected (usb.csv:1) and the archive plus raw CAD/firmware files were xcopied to E:\ (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:5, filemod.csv:2-4). Blast radius: the ENG-FS-01 IP_Designs data and the d.coleman identity; data left the org on removable media.
decoy: An internet scanner produced a failed-logon burst against the local Administrator from 203.0.113.240 (security.evtx.jsonl:2-4) and a sanctioned cloud-backup agent made outbound HTTPS to 52.95.110.10 (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:4, netflow.csv:1). Together they look like an external breach exfiltrating to the cloud, but the brute-force never succeeded (all 4625, rated benign threat_intel.csv:1) and 52.95.110.10 is the approved corporate backup endpoint (threat_intel.csv:2). A correct agent must self-correct to the insider-USB-exfil theory.
root_cause: A trusted insider collected engineering IP from a file share, staged it in an encrypted archive, and exfiltrated it to a personal USB drive - there was no external compromise.

expected_findings.label: Local data staging (encrypted archive of collected files)
Data exfiltration over USB removable media
